title: Put the lid back on a jack-o'-lantern: its key notch is under the lid, so it only drops in when turned to the tooth
instruction: Put the lid back on the jack-o'-lantern.
context: Carving a jack-o'-lantern is a common Halloween job at home, and the lid comes off again and again to light or check the candle. Carving guides say to cut the lid with the knife leaning inward, so it rests on a cone and cannot fall in, and to cut a key so it goes back only one way. Set back on the tooth, the lid rocks proud and lets the candle smoke the skin; pressing does nothing. It has to be turned until the key drops, and once the lid is over the opening the tooth is hidden under it.
setup: World: x away from the robot, y to its left, z up; bench top z 0.7475 m. Pumpkin (free on the bench): a carvable foam craft pumpkin ballasted to 0.80 kg 146 mm across at the widest, 105 mm from the bench to the rim of the opening at its top, flat 100 mm bottom, orange with ten ribs, a face (two eyes, nose, mouth) carved on one side. Its axis is at (0.300, 0.110) m. Opening: cut with the knife leaning 45 degrees inward, a cone 66 mm across at the rim and 36 mm across 15 mm down. On the side opposite the face a tooth 10 mm wide is left on the cut: there the cut surface stands 8 mm further in, the full 15 mm depth. Lid (ballasted to 0.030 kg), cut from the same wall: a cone 65 mm across at its top face and 41 mm at its bottom, 12 mm thick, the same 45-degree edge, with a notch 14 mm wide and 10 mm deep in its edge for the tooth; stem 15 mm across and 26 mm tall on its middle. Keyed, its top is level with the rim. Start: the lid rests on the opening with its notch turned away from the tooth, so it sits on the tooth about 5 mm proud and tilted. Lot A: face toward the robot (-x), tooth on the far side (+x); notch 110 degrees counterclockwise (from above) from the tooth. Lot B: pumpkin turned 90 degrees counterclockwise, face to the robot's right, tooth to its left; notch 75 degrees clockwise from the tooth. Lot C: pumpkin turned 55 degrees clockwise, face toward the robot and its left, tooth away and to its right; notch 155 degrees counterclockwise from the tooth. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, 1.0 when all of these hold together, with every gripper link and fingertip more than 5 mm from the lid and stem and the lid and pumpkin moving no more than 1 mm for 1 s: the lid's notch is within 8 degrees of the tooth about the opening's axis; the lid's top centre is within 2 mm of level with the rim; the lid is tilted under 3 degrees from the pumpkin's axis; and its centre is within 3 mm of the opening's axis. 0 otherwise, including a lid still held, resting on the tooth, hanging on the notch's edge, seated with the notch elsewhere, upside down or on the bench. Whole trial: if the pumpkin is ever pushed more than 10 mm or turned or tipped more than 5 degrees from where it started, if the lid ever falls in through the opening (top more than 20 mm below the rim), or if the hands, lid or pumpkin cannot be read at any step, the trial scores 0. Setting the lid down on the bench and then seating it is allowed. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 control steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz) per trial; trials on lots A, B and C, averaged (--epochs 3).
reset_notes: 1. Lift the lid off. 2. Turn the pumpkin on its tape mark (axis at x 0.300 m, y 0.110 m) so the face points the lot's way: lot A at the robot, lot B to the robot's right, lot C toward the robot turned 55 degrees to its left. 3. Set the lid on the opening with its notch turned from the tooth (opposite the face) by the lot's angle, seen from above: lot A 110 degrees counterclockwise, lot B 75 degrees clockwise, lot C 155 degrees counterclockwise, and let it rest on the tooth. Nothing is consumed; the foam pumpkin and lid are reused.
fidelity: True-size carvable foam craft pumpkin (about 140 mm), lid and cut; rigid bodies with real contact. The pumpkin is ballasted to 0.80 kg with a sand bag on its floor, and the lid to 30 g with a steel washer under the stem. Masses, wall and lid thickness, and friction 0.6 are estimates to measure on the stand-in; cut both to a printed template. Contact force is not scored.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (lots A, B, C each 1.0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A, B, C each 0.0; step limit in each). object_jitter=0, --epochs 3.
